title: Recovery before and after rescue immunotherapy
summary: A retrospective multicentre series records 18 treated attacks in 17 people with MOGAD or AQP4-positive NMOSD. IL-6 receptor blockade began within one month of attack nadir. Thirteen attacks were treated as acute escalation after inadequate earlier therapy; five represented early initiation of maintenance treatment.
purpose: Audience: a clinician. Use 180–240 words in English. Explain what the sequence supports and what it leaves unresolved about an acute rescue effect. Address attacks versus patients, the two treatment intentions, the improvement already present before blockade, and why the reported P values do not alone identify a causal effect. Give brief evidence-based justifications, not a private reasoning trace. Do not invent unreported findings, ages, test results or outcomes. Do not prescribe a dose or claim that an unreported result is normal.

case.initial_facts:
A retrospective multicentre series records 18 treated attacks in 17 people with MOGAD or AQP4-positive NMOSD. IL-6 receptor blockade began within one month of attack nadir. Thirteen attacks were treated as acute escalation after inadequate earlier therapy; five represented early initiation of maintenance treatment.
The authors report an EDSS improvement before IL-6 blockade, from a nadir median of 5.0 to a pre-blockade median of 3.5 (P=.001), and a further decrease to 2.0 at three months (P=.03 versus pre-blockade). These are the reported comparison summaries; the packet does not establish the participant subset for every paired comparison. There is no concurrent untreated control group. Earlier corticosteroids/plasma exchange and spontaneous recovery can affect the course.

case.hidden: The source reports visual-acuity outcomes, infections and other details that are not supplied. No patient-specific management decision or hidden final diagnosis is required.
case.reference: Do not count 18 attacks as 18 independent patients. Escalation and early-maintenance intentions differ. Improvement preceding blockade must not be attributed to blockade. Subsequent change is an association in a selected uncontrolled series, with prior therapy, natural recovery and subset uncertainty. Statistical significance is not a randomised causal contrast. Do not convert changes in an ordinal EDSS median into a validated percentage recovery.
